analysis.multiple_comparisons: none; all 54 registered rows, theorem obligations, and controls are conjunctive
ood_conditions: proof class fixed before anchor visibility
analysis.stopping_rule: bind manifest, source, and predecessor before the grid; process all 54 rows in frozen order; stop before later work on any mismatch, float/RNG use, 30-second wall limit, 64-MiB traced-Python peak, or one-MiB artifact limit
analysis.uncertainty: none; probabilities are exact rational consequences of the frozen product law

budget.execution: strictly sequential standard-library enumeration with no worker subprocesses or experiment RNG
budget.partial_run_policy: fail closed and emit no claim-eligible artifact

claim_boundary: the primary model is the frozen four-bit anchor R*=0011 with exact safe-acceptance bits and one-sided 0-to-1 noise only on its two hazard-rejection bits
the 2m hazard-bit replica errors are mutually independent Bernoulli(epsilon) coins in the declared bit-major replica-minor order
fresh_iid uses a new independent 2m-coin batch at each of exactly H post-install attack opportunities; persistent installs one batch and reuses it for all H opportunities
the installed anchor is visible before an adaptive adversary chooses one of exactly two proof classes and makes the registered hazard proposal
the registered finite grid is m in {1,3,5}, epsilon in {0,1/20,1/10}, H in {1,8,64}, and the two frozen temporal models
the perfect-correlation, false-negative-only, blinded-adversary, swapped-bit, epsilon-zero, and inherited safe-cycle cases are controls, not enlargements of the primary model

no claim about arbitrary learners, arbitrary or unknown correlation, two-sided or state-dependent error, learned evidence, infinite distinct-state progress, open-ended verifier replacement, general ASMP-5 systems, or resolution of ASMP-5
experimental_unit: one exact registered (m, epsilon, H, temporal-model) row; replica patterns and recurrence steps are terms of that row, not independent samples

hypotheses.falsifier: any registered row differs from the exact p_m, q_m, or temporal-risk formula, or either single-bit exploit witness fails
hypotheses.prediction: independent hazard-bit majorities and reveal-before-choice give q_m=1-(1-p_m)^2 and the registered finite-horizon risks

hypotheses.falsifier: for any finite odd m and positive probability epsilon the fresh risk does not tend to one, or persistent risk changes with positive H
hypotheses.prediction: fresh independent batches accumulate to eventual failure probability one, while one persistent batch retains risk q_m

hypotheses.falsifier: epsilon zero is nonzero-risk, false-negative-only noise reaches hazard, the inherited cycle is unsafe, or blinded/perfectly-correlated one-bit risk differs from p_m

changes.batch_reuse: fresh independent batch at every opportunity versus one persistent batch

changes.proof_class_timing: choose after visibility versus one fixed class chosen before visibility

denominators.registry_row: one frozen (m, epsilon, H, temporal-model) tuple
denominators.replica_pattern: one of exactly 2^(2m) ordered joint bit patterns

exposure.activation: both single-bit error fixtures install an accepting hazard bit
exposure.eligibility: all 2m independent replica coins and exactly H attack opportunities are represented
exposure.state_change: an installed erroneous hazard bit changes its class-specific hazard decision from reject to accept

model.error_law: all 2m replica coins are mutually independent Bernoulli(epsilon) false-positive indicators
model.code_hash: the required --source-commit contains byte-identical copies of exactly the eight source files
installation_and_attack_order: draw the registered replica batch when required by the temporal model
install each hazard bit as the strict majority of its m replicas while retaining both safe bits exactly
reveal the installed four-bit anchor to the adversary
let the adversary choose proof class 0 or 1
model.rng: no experiment RNG; the primary evaluates exact Fraction formulas and the verifier sums the complete finite coin space
model.update_order: install according to temporal law, reveal anchor, choose proof class, evaluate one hazard proposal, then advance the safe/failed state

question: How does a finite replicated one-sided anchor error propagate across repeated post-install adversarial opportunities under fresh and persistent temporal laws?

seed_plan.pairing: symbolic partitions only; no RNG sampling, statistical replicate, or adaptive outcome selection

theorem.fresh_infinite_horizon: for every finite odd m and 0<epsilon<=1, the failure probability tends to one
